The evidence of efficacy of PREZISTA/rtv is based on the analyses of 24-week data from 2 ongoing, randomized, controlled trials, TMC114-C213 and TMC114-C202, in antiretroviral treatment-experienced HIV-1 infected adult subjects.

These are ongoing randomized, controlled, Phase 2b trials consisting of 2 parts: an initial partially-blinded, dose-finding part and a second long-term part in which all subjects randomized to PREZISTA/rtv received the recommended dose of 600/100 mg b.i.d.

target_moa.text: Darunavir is an inhibitor of the HIV-1 protease; it selectively inhibits cleavage of HIV-encoded Gag-Pol polyproteins in infected cells, thereby preventing formation of mature virus particles.

citations.quote: Darunavir is an inhibitor of the HIV-1 protease. It selectively inhibits the cleavage of HIV encoded Gag-Pol polyproteins in infected cells, thereby preventing the formation of mature virus particles.
PREZISTA™ (darunavir) is an inhibitor of the human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) protease.

key_safety.text: Most common treatment-emergent adverse events (>10%) were diarrhea, nausea, headache, and nasopharyngitis; in the pooled randomized trials diarrhea 19.8% (vs 28.2% comparator), nausea 18.3% (vs 12.9%), headache 15.3% (vs 20.2%), and nasopharyngitis 13.7% (vs 10.5%). Severe skin rash, including erythema multiforme and Stevens-Johnson Syndrome, has been reported; rash of all grades occurred in 7% of subjects.

citations.quote: The most common treatment-emergent adverse events (> 10%) reported in the *de novo* subjects, regardless of causality or frequency, were diarrhea, nausea, headache, and nasopharyngitis.
diarrhea was reported in 19.8% and 28.2%, nausea in 18.3% and 12.9%, headache in 15.3% and 20.2%, and nasopharyngitis in 13.7% and 10.5%, of subjects, respectively.

During the clinical development program, severe skin rash, including erythema multiforme and Stevens-Johnson Syndrome, has been reported. In some cases, fever and elevations of transaminases have also been reported. In clinical trials (n=924), rash (all grades, regardless of causality) occurred in 7% of subjects treated with PREZISTA; the discontinuation rate due to rash was 0.3%.
